value.description: The amended ceiling in the pending proposal.

was.description: The prior value the confirmation shows as "(was …)" (adapters/governance.py:110-115). Recorded on the receipt the amendment finalises (receipts[].superseded_budgets, ADR-0072).

claimId.description: A claim identifier, the one claim-id pattern (shared-defs claimId); the terminal consent names a status the same way (core/evaluation.py:495-501).

configurationAmendment.description: The human amendment the confirm_amendment form confirms: ceilings only, the decision payload's own amendment shape (empirica/v2 request.schema.json governanceDecisionPayload.amendment) with each ceiling's prior value (the "(was …)" the form renders; run/4 records it as receipts[].superseded_budgets, ADR-0072).

configurationBudget.description: One budget row exactly as the dialog builds it (core/projection.py governance_dialog, budgets from governance.CEILINGS, core/governance.py:46-47; the shared dialog shape empirica/v2 shared-defs governancePresentation.dialog.budgets).

help.description: One of the core's help strings, display-escaped (the schema's top note).

label.description: One of the core's label strings, display-escaped (the schema's top note).

short.description: One of the core's short strings, display-escaped (the schema's top note).

then.description: A confirm_amendment document names the amendment it confirms; nothing else can answer it.
An approve document confirms the proposal as it stands, so it carries no amendment.

configurationDocument.description: What the "approve run configuration" and "confirm_amendment" forms ask (ADR-0063, ADR-0072): the whole sizing case — the explicit question, the goal, the unverified rationale, every budget with used and bounds, and on a confirm_amendment document the amendment with its priors.

budgets.description: Every ceiling in the dialog's order, pinned by position (review-2 #44): the dialog is built from governance.CEILINGS, so the rows are exactly max_passes, then max_spawns, then max_audit_spawns — once each, no fourth row. Each row's used is the same fact the form shows live; the document holds no separate used map (ADR-0072, review-1).

control_mode.description: The mode the decision authorises (the state schema's own control_mode, empirica/v2 state.schema.json:222-226): inside the proposal_digest the decision binds (core/governance.py:70-76) and later automatic acceptances depend on (ADR-0072).

goal.description: The run's goal in full, display-escaped (the schema's top note) — the form's first line, the document's whole text (the dialog goal, shared-defs governancePresentation.dialog.goal).

governance_state.description: The core's state word, carried as information beside the question (ADR-0072): pending on the approve form, revision_pending when a proposal was revised, rejected when a previous decision was refused and a re-present is admitted (HUMAN_WAIT_STATES, core/governance.py:189). It is not the form discriminator.

plan_revision.description: The dialog's epoch (the core's plan_revision, core/projection.py governance_dialog; each amendment bumps it, core/governance.py revise:128-146).

proposal_digest.description: The proposal the decision binds (governance proposal_digest, bound again by the governance decision payload).

question.description: The form's question, derived by the core, never the adapter (ADR-0072): confirm_amendment iff some receipt has outcome amend and plan_revision + 1 == governance.plan_revision, approve otherwise. The state word is not the discriminator: an amendment before the first approval parses governance_state pending (revise, core/governance.py:137-138), a later author revision yields revision_pending without a human amendment (core/evaluation.py:1607-1622), and rejected still admits a re-present (core/governance.py:189).

rationale.description: The sizing rationale moved here wholesale (the form renders all of it today, adapters/governance.py:88-93), display-escaped (the schema's top note); null when the proposal carries none. Shape copied from the dialog's rationale (shared-defs governancePresentation.dialog.rationale).

rationale_source.description: The rationale is the author's own sizing case, unverified wording (ADR-0063's unverified label, the one the forms render under today): the document says so, so untrusted text cannot read as a core statement.

run_id.description: The run the decisions name (the decision payloads' run_id).

contextWhenShown.description: Context when the document is shown, NOT part of the decision (ADR-0072): it explains what the dialog stood beside. It is inside the digested document only because the invocation facts are fixed for the run's lifetime — recorded at StartRun and never rewritten afterwards — so the digest cannot change between the fetch, present and the decision. Nothing volatile is here: a present receipt changes the reviews left (application/governance.py:96-101, counted at core/governance.py:168-177), the host's answer rewrites human_surface (application/transaction.py:417-419), and each budget's used count is already on its budget row (the form shows the numbers live instead).

digest256.description: A sha256 content digest, the same pattern every other empirica/v2 schema uses (shared-defs digest256; core/canonical.py:34-37).

evidenceClaim.description: One claim of the batch with its text, display-escaped (the schema's top note) — the item text that moves out of the form (adapters/confirmation.py:131-134); id, wording digest and text from the argument view's claim row (core/projection.py:566-573).

claim_digest.description: The claim's wording digest, binding id and text (core/evaluation.py claim_digest:277-280).

text.description: The claim's full text, display-escaped (the schema's top note).

then.description: The terminal consent is one decision on one item: it holds nothing else (core/evaluation.py terminal_batch:495-501).

evidenceDocument.description: What the end-of-pass evidence batch asks, and the terminal "end this run without converging" consent: every record with its claim text, quote, class, outcome and why-no-spike reason, and every claim with its text (ADR-0067, ADR-0072).

claims.description: The batch's waiting decisions first, in graph order (core/evaluation.py confirmation_batch).

key.description: The batch's key — derivations and exactly the shown items (core/evaluation.py confirmation_batch:549-561; the terminal batch's own key, terminal_key:486-492) — the value the evidence presentation payload carries.

records.description: The batch's records, in their claim's graph order then submission (core/evaluation.py confirmation_batch).

run_id.description: The run the presentation and the confirmation name (the evidence payloads' run_id).

evidenceRecord.description: One research record of the batch, from the argument view's research artifacts (core/projection.py:576-591) as the items builder reads them (adapters/confirmation.py build_items:136-155); the confirmation artifact body's own record_id word (core/evaluation.py:1029-1035). Review-1: a human cannot judge a quote without the claim it answers and whether the record claims to support or refute it, so the claim text and outcome ride with the record.

citation.description: The quote a human confirms or rejects, display-escaped (the schema's top note) — the research payload's citation; the only record fact the form keeps.

claim_digest.description: The claim wording the record is bound to (the argument artifact's claim_digest), binding the claim_text's id and text (core/evaluation.py:277-280).

claim_text.description: The claim's own text the record answers, display-escaped (the schema's top note) — the content a human must read to judge the quote against what it claims to establish (ADR-0072, review-1); its id and text are the claim_digest the record carries.

outcome.description: The record's own outcome: supporting when the research action's result was supports, refuting otherwise (core/evaluation.py:1590; the action vocabulary, empirica/v2 request.schema.json:713-717; public-contract artifact_outcomes' research pair).

record_id.description: The record's artifact id (the argument artifact_id; the batch's record_ids).

source_kind.description: The record's immutable source kind (the research payload's source_kind, empirica/v2 public-contract.json:584-590).

source_ref.description: Where the record's fact comes from (the research payload's source_ref), display-escaped as free text (the schema's top note).

spike_unavailable.description: Why no deterministic check can establish the record (the research payload's spike_unavailable; empirica/v2 public-contract.json:618-620), display-escaped (the schema's top note) — the "why no spike" reason that moves out of the form (adapters/confirmation.py:153-155).

verification_class.description: How the record is verified, derived from source_ref (core/citations.py verification_class:66-73): null when no class can be derived.

invocationFacts.description: The run-fixed invocation facts, the five the ADR keeps in the digested document (ADR-0072; the shown facts are INVOCATION_FACTS, core/projection.py:299-305; types copied from the state schema's invocation, empirica/v2 state.schema.json:755-877). human_surface is deliberately absent: the host's own answer rewrites it between calls (application/transaction.py:417-419), and nothing that can change is digested — the document is a pure function of run state.

host.description: The executing host's name, display-escaped as free text (the schema's top note).

signal.description: What started the run, display-escaped as free text (the schema's top note).

terminalConsent.description: The terminal "end this run without converging" consent (ADR-0063's amendment, ADR-0072): the batch terminal member (core/evaluation.py terminal_batch:495-501) with what ending now would leave unresolved.

digest.description: The consent's wording digest (the terminal batch's terminal.digest, core/evaluation.py terminal_batch).

residuals.description: What ending now leaves unresolved: the run's active obligation rows, excluding the terminal consent row itself, selected by one core function from a GetRun-shaped snapshot (ADR-0072; core/projection.py _obligation:139-147).

required.description: The obligation row's required line, display-escaped (the schema's top note).

status.description: The status the run would end as (TERMINAL_STATUSES, core/evaluation.py:456).

description: Source-tree schema (not vendored into the plugin; ADR-0072) of the core-owned immutable JSON document a human decides on: what the native forms moved out and the record binds by its digest. The bytes are pinned by the contract validator: json.dumps(doc, sort_keys=True, indent=2, ensure_ascii=False) plus one trailing newline, UTF-8; the document_digest is the SHA-256 of exactly those bytes. Field names and types are derived from the builders that render this content today, cited per field. Every free-text value is display-escaped by the core's one escaper (safe_text, core/projection.py:287-293) — a backslash doubled, bidi and zero-width characters turned into \uXXXX — so a text-direction override can never reach the file a human opens; the raw wording stays bound by its digests, which are computed before the document is built. The document is a pure function of run state: no wall-clock times and nothing the adapter chooses (a receipt id the host generates is never here), and no value the human's own answer or the host's surface observation can change — nothing volatile is digested, or the core's recompute at the decision would refuse every decision.
title: Empirica v2 human-in-the-loop document (empirica.hitl/1)
